items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: I'll tell you, I mean, all of them -- Klook, old man Max, Joe Jones ...

ctx.x: Everybody that had lived in Chicago, or seems, almost passed through Chicago, knows something about Ike Day. He's become almost a legend. Tell us about him.

He was a legend. Every drummer that ever came to Chicago would find Ike. Ike had his problems, but he was young and phenomenal. He was upsetting. That was during the days when, like I said, Red Saunders was one of the top drummers out there in Chicago. But the Delisa Club would have on Monday mornings would have a breakfast dance, after the last show at 4 o'clock. The breakfast dance started about five.

Ike might come in there and Red would let him sit in, and they had this great big, hydraulic stage and Red had maybe about 15 pieces up there. And Ike'd come up there and start soloing, and then -- they had those little wooden beaters, and people would beat along with the music, but they wouldn't beat along with Ike when he was playing drums. You could hear a pin drop when he was soloing, he was so beautiful.

items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: Max's Ornette's group and Arnett's group, Coleman Hawkins, Old Man Joe Jones, Kenny Dorham... [were] getting a bunch of groups together to go and play Newport

ctx.x: It don't make sense. Then, on top of that, you got to keep up your other dues at your home local. But that's the way it went down. Anyway, they got me fined, and Johnny Griffin had a week at the Regal, a big band, you know, he wanted me to come in with him. But they wouldn't let me play. So I'm stuck in Chicago; I can't work, and I wound up pawning the fiddle that he bought me; started bumming around, drinking and carrying on. And I stayed out there until I just got tired, and in the summer of 1960, Walter…

Eager, a tenor player, a white boy -- and they were getting a bunch of groups together to go and play Newport, and Max's Ornette's group and Arnett's group, Coleman Hawkins, Old Man Joe Jones, Kenny Dorham, King Durham, Kenny Drew, Arthur Taylor, Abdul-Malik, Baby Lawrence, the dancer.
